title: Drafting a cheque bounce notice without the mistakes that kill a case
p1:
A cheque bounce notice can look simple. But one small mistake in drafting it can weaken a case before it even reaches court.

Many people think sending a notice is just a formality after a cheque is dishonoured. That is the first mistake.
p2:
A surprising fact: the notice is not just a warning to the drawer. It is a legal step with specific requirements. Missing key details, incorrect timelines, or unclear demands can create avoidable problems later.

The notice must clearly mention the cheque details, the reason for dishonour, the amount due, and the demand for payment within the required period.
p3:
The practical takeaway is simple: a strong cheque bounce notice is not about using complicated legal words. It is about accuracy, clarity, and following the right process.

Before sending any notice, check whether every important fact matches your documents. A small drafting error today can become a bigger legal challenge tomorrow.
